sections.title: Molecular profile of ovarian endometrioid carcinoma
sections.intro: OEC is an **endometrial-type carcinoma that happens to sit in the ovary**: WNT (CTNNB1), PI3K (PIK3CA, PTEN) and ARID1A mutations dominate, most tumours are hormone-receptor positive, and most present at stage I–II. The endometrial molecular classification applies and separates prognosis as it does in the uterus [1–5], but **no trial has used it to select treatment in OEC**. **Pathology in brief.** Grade 3 is the diagnostic trap. On morphology alone, pathologists agreed on grade 3 endometrioid vs HGSC in 69% of cases, rising to 96% with WT1/p53 immunohistochemistry; WT1-negative grade 3 OEC had the same immunophenotype and survival as grade 2 (HR 1.07, 0.39–3.21) [6]. Many historically diagnosed "high-grade endometrioid" tumours were HGSC, which is why the largest genomic series required WT1 negativity [7]. None of the trial texts read for this note mentions WT1, so their "high-grade endometrioid" patients were defined by local histology. Synchronous endometrial and ovarian endometrioid carcinomas are clonally related in almost all cases (17 of 18 [8]; all 22 sporadic pairs [9]), yet organ-confined low-grade pairs behave indolently, as independent early primaries would [8].

notes.title: Practical consequence for testing
notes.md:
1. **MMR IHC on every OEC.** It is the commonest actionable result (about 1 in 7), it flags Lynch syndrome (MSH2/MSH6 loss is frequent [12]), and it is the only route to immunotherapy in recurrent OEC (T3B), which rests on tumour-agnostic data only.
2. **p53 and POLE complete the molecular class.** p53abn OEC carries the worst prognosis (median OS 4.7 yr) [1]; POLEmut had no progression events in pooled data [5]. Neither result has been tested as a treatment selector in OEC.
3. **Grade 3 or p53-abnormal "endometrioid" → ask for WT1.** A WT1-positive, p53-abnormal tumour is HGSC and belongs in OVCA_HGSC_Algorithm_v1.2. A WT1-negative p53abn tumour is p53abn OEC, the class with the worst OEC prognosis [1].
4. **BRCA1/2 (germline and tumour) and HRD** for high-grade OEC at stage III–IV, before the maintenance decision (T2B). The HRD-positive fraction in OEC is unknown.
5. **ER/PR** is prognostic in OEC [10] and is the entry test for endocrine therapy; ER/PR intensity did not predict benefit in PARAGON or LACOG 1018 [22,23].
6. **FRα-high is rare (about 6%)** [19]; mirvetuximab was not tested in OEC.

notes.title: Reading Table 1
notes.md:
- **No randomized result is specific to OEC.** OEC was 21–27% of the early-stage trials, and the only OEC effect estimate is GOG-157's exploratory 6-vs-3-cycle HR of **1.07 (0.47–2.44)** [30]: there is no signal that OEC needs more than 3 cycles. In ICON1 + ACTION the chemotherapy effect did not differ by cell type (P=.55) [25], but those trials predate WT1-based histotyping and mixed incompletely staged patients, in whom the benefit was concentrated (ACTION) [27].
- **Stage IA/IB grade 1–2 OEC was not eligible for GOG-157 or GOG-175, and IA/IB grade 1 was not eligible for ACTION** [27,29,31]; only ICON1 admitted any stage I–II when the clinician was uncertain [26]. The case for chemotherapy in low-grade IA/IB OEC therefore rests on observational data, which show **no survival association** (Oseledchyk overall; Yu IA/IB) [33,34]. The one consistent observational signal is **stage IC, grade 3** (HR 0.583) [33].
- Real-world practice is more aggressive than this evidence: in a 721-case centrally reviewed OEC cohort, 68.0% (398/585) of FIGO I/II patients received chemotherapy; in pT1–2 without macroscopic residual disease chemotherapy was independently associated with better disease-specific survival (HR 0.42, 0.21–0.88; p=0.0219), with no benefit seen in G1 pT1a/b (retrospective, selection bias acknowledged) [35].
- **Molecular class has not been tested as an adjuvant selector in OEC.** p53abn (worst prognosis) and POLEmut (no recurrences) are the obvious candidates for escalation and de-escalation [1,5]; applying PORTEC-3-style class-directed logic from EMCA_Endometrioid_Algorithm_v1.2 is extrapolation.

notes.title: Reading Table 2A
notes.md:
1. **Every row is an HGSC result.** OEC was 0.7–12% of these trials, and only iPocc reports a histology subgroup that includes it, pooled with serous (HR 0.81) [47]. Carboplatin–paclitaxel is the OEC backbone by default, not by OEC-specific evidence.
2. **The trial most enriched for OEC was JGOG-3016 (12%)**, and its OEC patients sit inside the "serous or other" subgroup that drove the dose-dense benefit [39]. That does not make dose-dense paclitaxel an OEC recommendation; the trial did not break OEC out, and the Western trials were negative (see HGSC Table 2A).
3. **Advanced OEC is uncommon and molecularly mixed.** Stage III/IV was 48% of TP53-mutant OEC but a minority of CTNNB1-mutant OEC [7]. A p53abn stage III OEC and a low-grade CTNNB1-mutant stage III OEC are unlikely to share a chemotherapy sensitivity, but no trial has tested this.

notes.title: The first-line maintenance decision in OEC
notes.md:
- **Only high-grade OEC was eligible for the PARPi trials, and it was 0.5–3% of them** (SOLO1 2%, PAOLA-1 2.5%, PRIMA 2.7%, ATHENA-MONO 2.6%, DUO-O 2.1%) [51,53,55,57,60]. No trial reports an OEC subgroup, and eligibility used local histology without WT1 (see molecular section). The OEC PARPi decision is therefore an **extrapolation from the biomarker, not from histology**: a BRCA1/2-mutated or HRD-positive high-grade OEC is treated on the HGSC evidence (OVCA_HGSC_Algorithm_v1.2 Table 2B).
- **BRCA1/2 mutations occur in OEC** (12.5% by WES, often with TP53 mutation [7]), so testing high-grade stage III–IV OEC is not wasted. How often OEC is HRD-positive without BRCA is unknown.
- **Low-grade stage III–IV OEC has no maintenance evidence at all.** PARPi trials required high grade; VELIA excluded all non-serous [58]; IO trials were negative overall [63,64]. Endocrine maintenance is biologically attractive (ER+ 77%, PR+ 67%, hormone-receptor positivity prognostic with HR 0.33 [10]) but the letrozole maintenance data are low-grade serous only [65].
- **MMRd OEC in first line:** none of the first-line IO trials reports MMR status, and the one with an endometrioid grade breakdown (IMagyn050, 35 patients) was negative overall [63]. Endometrial dMMR first-line IO results do not transfer by default.

sections.title: 3. Recurrent disease
sections.intro: The platinum-free interval decides the regimen class, as in HGSC. **3A** = relapse ≥6 months after last platinum; **3B** = relapse <6 months. Every row carries a `Prior systemic therapy` column.

notes.title: Two boundaries in recurrent OEC
notes.md:
1. **OEC was 2–8% of the recurrence trials, and no randomized trial reports an OEC effect estimate.** The only OEC-specific recurrence result is negative: pembrolizumab monotherapy produced **0 responses in 28 endometrioid patients** (ORR 0.0%, 0.0–12.3) in KEYNOTE-100, unselected for MMR [87].
2. **Treatment that selects on a biomarker rather than histology is the realistic OEC path:** MMRd → pembrolizumab (tumour-agnostic, 15 ovarian patients) [15]; BRCAm → PARPi maintenance; HER2 3+ → T-DXd [18]; ER/PR+ → endocrine therapy (tiny OEC numbers) [22,23]. FRα-high is rare in OEC [19].

notes.title: Reading notes for 3A
notes.md:
- **Platinum re-induction ± bevacizumab** is OEC standard only by inclusion: OEC was 5–8% of CALYPSO, OCEANS, GOG-0213 and MITO-16B [66,67,69,70].
- **PARPi maintenance in recurrent OEC requires the biomarker, not the histology label.** SOLO2 (gBRCAm, 5.8% endometrioid) and ARIEL3 (4.1%) admitted high-grade OEC [72,74]; Study 19 did not [71]. Final OS was not significant in either (see HGSC Table 3A).
- **Do not substitute a PARPi for chemotherapy**: SOLO3 OS null, ARIEL4 OS worse [77,79].
- **Endocrine therapy after CA125 progression** (PARAGON) gave durable benefit in a minority (22% on treatment >6 months) but only 4 endometrioid patients were enrolled [23]. No low-grade OEC endocrine series was found.

notes.title: Platinum-resistant OEC
notes.md:
1. **No platinum-resistant option has OEC-specific randomized evidence.** OEC was ≤8% of each trial; MIRASOL excluded it [21]; ROSELLA's only non-HGSC signal is 10 patients pooled with carcinosarcoma [81].
2. **Checkpoint inhibitors need MMRd.** Unselected OEC did not respond to pembrolizumab (0/28) [87], whereas MSI-H/dMMR ovarian cancer responded in 33.3% (15 patients, histotypes not reported) [15]. With about 14% of OEC MMRd [1], this is the most important test to have before platinum resistance.
3. **KEYNOTE-B96 is the only positive IO combination that admitted any-grade OEC** (13 patients) [16]; its benefit was confined to CPS ≥1, and CPS in OEC is unknown.
4. **Endocrine therapy** has only case-level OEC representation (2 patients in LACOG 1018, 4 in PARAGON) [22,23]; hormone-receptor intensity did not predict benefit in either.

notes.title: Reading Table 4
notes.md:
- **OEC was 1.6–4.3% of the NACT and HIPEC trials**, so non-inferiority of NACT and the OVHIPEC-1 OS benefit are HGSC results [88,89,91,94].
- **OEC had the best prognosis of any histotype in EORTC 55971** (post hoc) [88], and most OEC present at stage I–II (78% in the WES series); in that series 14 of the 29 TP53-mutant tumours were stage III/IV, against 11% of CTNNB1-mutant tumours [7].
- In a national registry, **non-HGSC tumours failed to reach interval surgery after NACT more often than HGSC (36% vs 25%)** [96]. This is not OEC-specific, but it argues for primary cytoreduction when complete resection is feasible in a non-HGSC tumour.
